He was crossing a parking lot when a bolt hit nearby and the current jumped through him, throwing him to the ground. 05_venezuela-earthquake-rescue-2026.json.script: Buried Alive For Eight Days? When Venezuela's twin earthquakes leveled a shopping mall in La Guaira, the whole parking structure came down — except one thing: a tiny security booth, and the guard still inside it. Hernan Gil Flores spent eight days trapped in that pocket of space while 29 feet of concrete crushed everything around him. Rescuers lowered water and nutrients down a narrow shaft just to keep him alive, talking to him through a telescopic camera while international crews from Chile, Costa Rica, the U.S., Portugal, and Mexico spent three straight days tunneling toward him. Your AirPods battery is glued inside a sealed plastic shell with zero screws. Try to open them and you destroy them. iFixit gave every AirPods model a repairability score of 0 out of 10. Officially disposable by design.

After roughly 2 years the battery dies. From the first generation the story has been identical. Glued batteries, sealed housings, components buried under adhesive.

Apple charges $49 per earbud for battery service. They just hand you a replacement pair. That is not a repair. That is a subscription disguised as a product.

So on Tuesday I hid my phone inside a stuffed animal on the shelf and left for work like normal. Four hours later I sat in the parking lot with my hands shaking and watched the footage. He let himself in at 1:47, walked straight to my closet, and started going through my laundry basket, taking pictures of my things with his phone. I called the police right there in the lot. When they pulled his rental records, they found seventeen other tenants across three of his buildings who had filed the exact same complaint and were told there was no evidence. Then the officer turned his laptop around and showed me a folder labeled with all our names. Mine was the only one still empty.

03_textcard-shrinkflation.json.title: Your groceries didn't get more expensive - they got smaller
03_textcard-shrinkflation.json.text:
That bag of chips you buy every week is quietly shrinking. Same price, same packaging, roughly ten percent less inside. It is called shrinkflation, and in the last two years it has hit almost every product on the shelf.

Companies bank on one thing: you check the price, you never check the weight. A roll of paper towels quietly drops from 60 sheets to 54. A cereal box loses a few ounces. Nobody notices, and the margin grows.

You are paying the same money for less product on every single trip. That is not inflation. That is a price hike they hoped you would never see.
highlights: paying the same money for less

04_textcard-printer-ink.json.title: Printer ink is one of the most expensive liquids you can buy
04_textcard-printer-ink.json.text:
Drop for drop, printer ink costs more than fine champagne, more than premium vodka, and by some measures more than human blood. A tiny cartridge with a few milliliters inside can run you 30 or 40 dollars.

That works out to over 2,000 dollars per gallon. The printer itself is often sold at a loss, sometimes cheaper than one full set of replacement cartridges. The machine is bait. The ink is the trap.

And many printers now block cheaper third-party cartridges with firmware updates, just so you have to buy theirs. You do not own that printer. You are renting the right to use it.
